system.description:
Locking eyes with a beast, you pour your consciousness into it and thrust its weaker spirit aside; your own body slumps into a comatose state while your soul rides the animal as a living vessel.

Gaze into the eyes of the animal (it must have eyes) and expend Social Traits to enter its body — the more you spend, the deeper the connection: one Trait grants simple possession, with further Traits letting you also wield some of your own Disciplines (Auspex at two, Presence and Animalism at three, and so on). You are bound by the animal's physical limits but may use its natural weapons, and no distance limits your control. Injury to the animal inflicts equal sympathetic injury on your comatose body; if the beast is slain your soul returns and you enter torpor. Each Social Trait spent leaves one Negative Trait: Feral, which lingers (and should be roleplayed) until bought off one-for-one with Willpower Traits. Returning to your own body must be declared at the start of a turn; if you are injured while returning, make a Simple Test — a tie leaves you animalistic for the scene and a loss triggers immediate frenzy, though you return to your own form either way. Retest with Animal Ken.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines
